scope: Bounded IPC and lifecycle prerequisite for the existing passive desktop voice floater; not a complete in-game overlay.
implementation: Overlay snapshots are explicitly projected and validated for finite settings, known corner, bounded text/URLs, unique participants and a maximum of 64 participants. The client producer caps the list at the same bound. Malformed frames do not mutate the overlay.
Only the main application window's main frame can send overlay snapshots or invoke the six registered-game IPC operations; other frames cannot trigger the executable picker or registry operations.
The BrowserWindow starts hidden. Deferred delivery reads the latest snapshot, cannot resurrect a disabled/closed window and reuses one load listener even through repeated enable/disable cycles.

The overlay entry explicitly loads its stylesheet. Its content fills the fixed viewport and aligns the widget and scale origin to the selected corner. Renderer subscriptions now return a cleanup callback that removes their exact IPC listener on unmount.
verification: Agent and parent Electron TypeScript compilation and all 97 native tests passed, including parser, trusted-frame and fake-window lifecycle regressions.

Parent focused actual-renderer, subscription cleanup and preview tests passed: 3 files, 11 tests. Follow-up client typecheck caught an incomplete Electron bridge test mock; it was replaced by a scoped global stub, then client typecheck and scoped lint passed.

Follow-up parent Electron compilation and all 103 tests passed after adding optional widget controls and screen-workarea geometry. Size/position are computed before display; zero capacity hides the window, and physical capacity changes only the outgoing snapshot rather than saved preferences.
open: Real Windows display/window lifecycle and multi-monitor acceptance
Actual game-aware overlay, remaining widget controls and full P11 acceptance
release: No process injection, game launch, production publication or actual game-window acceptance claim.
